chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah, from Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from Samāʿah, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who slept through the salat (prayer) until the sun rose. He said: He should perform the two rakʿahs, then perform the morning salat (prayer).

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two rakʿahs, referring here to the two-unit prayer to be performed first
key_terms.طَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ: the sun rose; meaning the prayer time had passed
key_terms.نَامَ: slept; indicating missing the prayer due to sleep

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he sleeps through Fajr until after sunrise?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling for one who oversleeps and misses the time of the morning salat (prayer) until after sunrise. It indicates that he first performs the two rakʿahs and then performs the ghadāh, showing an order in making up what was missed.
